conventions: Design review: check mvp_compliance.E003 is raised when either list setting is a str; one test case per setting, asserted by id

Design review: an entry of the exempt-URLs setting is compared a path segment at a time against request.path_info; '/' covers every address and an empty entry covers nothing. The demo lists NO address
Design review: the permission is asked only of a user the outstanding query has just said would be stopped, and the answer is never stored in the session (decisions.md D15)
Design review: the interval comparison is now minus the stored timestamp against the CURRENT setting; with 0 nothing is stored. No separate 'honour nothing' rule
Design review: never assert the session key's name alone; compare the session's contents before and after as a whole

The permission goes in Document.Meta.permissions. Delete migration 0002 and regenerate it with makemigrations so the branch still adds exactly one migration holding the field and the permission; keep its name stable if you can. tests/test_migrations.py::TestEnforcedColumn must still pass unmodified
Seed accounts follow the demo's existing pattern: <role>.user@example.com, password 'password'. Read seed_demo before adding to it
docs/enforcement.md says: name only accounts whose sign-in value the holder cannot change, and remove a name when its account is removed

Repo standards that reviews have missed before: no leading-underscore names anywhere (functions, methods, attributes, modules, constants); line length 88; no compatibility aliases; no test of text content or wording; no test of layout or appearance
A mechanism an experienced Django developer would recognise beats a clever one: no dataclass, registry or settings object where a plain getattr(settings, NAME, default) at the point of use does
Settings are read with getattr at the point of use, as views.py reads MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_REDIRECT_URL
Every user-facing string is wrapped for translation and none says 'compliant', 'compliance' or names a regulation
Every model field carries verbose_name and help_text
Text for GitHub and docs is written for an outside contributor: plain words, no mention of agents, stages or tooling
